name: Review a code folder
description:
A careful colleague's review of a folder of code: a short summary, each real problem with its file and line, how serious it is, what goes wrong and a suggested fix, and what the code does well. It reads the code without running it and reports only problems it can point to in a line.

It works on the folder you choose when you launch it: a folder in this project, or one you pick from your computer. It never runs or changes the code. No code to hand? Try it on the sample, a small to-do app.
triggers: what is wrong with this code

source.title: Code folder
source.description: The folder of code to review: a folder in this project, or one you pick from your computer.

workPath.title: Working folder
workPath.description: Per-task working folder in the artifacts drawer. Defaults to this task's own folder so runs never collide; override with a stable name when you deliberately want runs to share files.

steps.name: Review the code
steps.description: Read the code and write a review of the real problems in it.
steps.prompt:
Review the code in the `source` input the way a careful colleague would, and write the review to `{{workPath}}/review.md`.

1. Open the file list `{{task.dir}}/inputs/source.json` with `read_artifact`. It lists every file in the folder and the drawer they are in.
2. Read every source file and test with the tool named on the `source` line under Invocation parameters. If there are more than 20, read the entry point and the files it uses first, 20 at most.
3. Look for real defects. Follow one concrete input through each function: does it return the right thing, change the right item, save what it changed, wait for what it starts, and handle the errors it can hit? Watch for counting that is off by one, a missing `await`, a change that is never saved, an error that is swallowed, input that is never checked, and a crash on an empty or missing value.
4. Write `{{workPath}}/review.md` with `write_artifact`, under exactly these three headings:
   - `## Summary`: two or three sentences on what the code does and how sound it is.
   - `## Findings`: one entry per real problem, the most serious first. Give each one its file and line (`path/to/file.js:12`), a severity of high, medium or low, what goes wrong with a concrete example, and a suggested fix. If you find no real problem, write `No problems found.`
   - `## What is good`: two or three things the code does well.

Report only problems you can point to in a line of the code you read. Never invent a file, a line or a bug, and do not pad the list: one real finding beats five guesses.

If the folder holds no file you can read, do not write `review.md`. Write a task note with `write_task_note` that says what you found, then end your turn.

checks.label: a finding that names its file and line, or "No problems found."
a severity of high, medium or low on the findings

steps.name: Finish
steps.description: The deliverable passed its checks. Stamp a short summary and report DONE.
steps.prompt: The deliverable passed its checks. Write a one-paragraph DONE summary to task notes via `write_task_note`: what you made, the deliverable path(s), and a one-line confirmation that each required section is there. Then report DONE.
